Claim_Summary: Support is overloaded and breaching SLA commitments.
Quote_or_Evidence: "We take somewhere north of five hundred tickets a week now and we have six agents. Our service agreement says first response inside two hours and we are averaging somewhere between eight and twelve."
Test_With_Data: T04: quantify weekly volume, first-response distribution, SLA breach proxy from development_tickets.json history.
Notes: Primary evidence for pain/urgency; aligns with brief baseline.

Claim_Summary: Prior fixes (hiring, canned responses, outsourcing) did not sustainably solve the problem.
Quote_or_Evidence: "We hired two people last year. It helped for about a month and then volume caught up. We tried a canned response library, which the agents hated because finding the right one took longer than writing the answer. We looked at outsourcing tier one and the quotes were more than my entire team costs."
Test_With_Data: T04: no direct dataset test; treat as contextual evidence for solution constraints (must reduce effort, not add findability burden).
Notes: Supports need for retrieval-assisted workflow rather than static canned responses.

Claim_Summary: Desired outcome is answering easy tickets so humans focus on hard ones; response time must improve without headcount.
Quote_or_Evidence: "I picture it answering the easy ones so my people can do the hard ones... What I need is for the response time number to come down without me asking for three more headcount that I am not going to get."
Test_With_Data: T04: estimate share of easy/doc-answerable tickets and potential automation/escalation split by intent/channel.
Notes: Frames business goal; must be reconciled with safe escalation.

Claim_Summary: FCR is more important than response time due to rework/cost; current FCR ~42%, target benchmark ~65%.
Quote_or_Evidence: "first contact resolution, if I am being honest, more than response time... every ticket that bounces to tier two costs us roughly four times what a resolved one costs... We are at forty-two per cent. The industry benchmark people quote at me is sixty-five."
Test_With_Data: T04: compute baseline FCR and escalation/repeat-contact proxies from history; segment by intent/channel/tier.
Notes: Key business metric for evaluation/reporting.

Claim_Summary: Wrong answers to customers are unacceptable; system must not create extra agent work.
Quote_or_Evidence: "If it sends something wrong to a customer... I would rather it said nothing than said something wrong. The second failure would be if it makes more work for the agents than it saves..."
Test_With_Data: T04/T26: measure guardrail blocks, escalation-with-context quality proxies, unsupported-claim risks; governance tests in build/eval.
Notes: Directly informs routing thresholds, guardrails, escalation design.

Claim_Summary: Leadership lacks ticket breakdown despite having data.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Do you know what your tickets are actually about? ... Broadly. Authentication, deployment problems, billing questions, API questions. If you asked me for a breakdown I would be guessing. We have the data, we have never really sat down with it."
Test_With_Data: T04: produce intent/urgency/channel/tier/region/language breakdowns from development_tickets.json.
Notes: Motivates data profiling as discovery evidence.

Claim_Summary: Enterprise SLA differences and explainability/compliance requirements are constraints.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Enterprise customers have a different agreement and they will notice immediately if they get worse service than they were getting. And I have a compliance review in the autumn, so whatever we do has to be explainable. I need to be able to say why it did what it did."
Test_With_Data: T04: segment outcomes by customer_tier; T31+: ensure decision logging/auditability and fairness analysis.
Notes: Supports tier-aware analysis and full decision logs.

Claim_Summary: Queue volume and triage pressure are high, especially Mondays; agents sort by age/SLA risk.
Quote_or_Evidence: "I open the queue and it is somewhere between forty and seventy tickets depending on the day. Mondays are worst. I sort by age because the oldest ones are the ones about to breach, and then I just work down."
Test_With_Data: T04: analyze received_at/channel distributions and response-time baseline proxies (if derivable).
Notes: Context for urgency/prioritization needs.

Claim_Summary: Many tickets are repetitive/known; a large share can be answered from prior experience.
Quote_or_Evidence: "If it is one I have seen before, four or five minutes. If it is something unusual, it can be forty minutes and then I escalate it anyway... I would say seven out of ten I could answer without looking anything up, because I have answered the same question that month already. Password lockouts, rate limits, why is my invoice higher, my deployment keeps rolling back. The same ones over and over."
Test_With_Data: T04: quantify answerable_from_docs and expected auto-respond rates; compare to 70% claim and to actual escalation/FCR outcomes (C1).
Notes: Potentially supports 'answers exist but delivery/findability fails' hypothesis; must be tested against data.

Claim_Summary: Time is lost finding and writing answers; documentation search is painful so agents use personal snippet files.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Finding it and writing it out. We have documentation, and it is good documentation, but searching it is painful, so most of us do not. I have a personal file of answers I have written before and I copy from that. Everyone has their own. Daniel has one too, and his is better than mine."
Test_With_Data: T04/T05: test corpus coverage vs ticket intents and retrieval needs; assess doc-answerable tickets that still escalated or took long (where available).
Notes: Critical evidence for retrieval/findability and knowledge reuse problem.

Claim_Summary: Escalation drivers include lack of knowledge, lack of confidence, and mandatory security escalation.
Quote_or_Evidence: "I do not know the answer. Or I think I know but I am not confident enough to send it... Or it is a security thing, which we are told to escalate every time regardless."
Test_With_Data: T04: analyze escalated tickets by intent/answerable_from_docs/must_not_auto_respond/security-related labels; compare avoidable vs required escalations (C2).
Notes: Supports escalation-with-context and policy-based forced escalation.

Claim_Summary: Assistive automation (draft + relevant page) would save time; fear of wrong automated answers creating downstream work.
Quote_or_Evidence: "I am worried it will send a wrong answer and I will be the one who picks up the angry follow-up... If it hands me a ticket with a draft and the relevant page attached, that would genuinely help. That would save me half of every ticket."
Test_With_Data: T04/T26: evaluate escalation payload usefulness and auto-answer risk trade-offs; include in PRD scope/options.
Notes: Important for defining escalation as valuable output, not only auto-response.

Claim_Summary: Non-fluent English customers take longer and have worse satisfaction; issue may be unnoticed.
Quote_or_Evidence: "The ones where English is not their first language take longer, because I have to work out what they are actually asking before I can answer it... Those tickets have our worst satisfaction scores and I do not think anyone has noticed."
Test_With_Data: T04: segment CSAT, resolution time, escalation/repeat contact by language_fluency and intersections (C3).
Notes: Key evidence for fairness audit hypotheses.

Claim_Summary: A large share of escalations may be avoidable (confidence/findability rather than true complexity).
Quote_or_Evidence: "In practice, about half of what reaches me is something tier one could have resolved if they had been confident, or if they had found the right page. The other half is genuinely hard..."
Test_With_Data: T04: measure avoidable-escalation proxy among escalated tickets using answerable_from_docs, expected_route, intent and must_not_auto_respond (C2).
Notes: Challenges assumption that escalations are mostly hard cases.

Claim_Summary: Escalations lack context, causing rework and customer frustration.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Usually just the original ticket, forwarded. No summary, no note about what was already tried... the first thing I do is read the whole thread and often ask the customer something they were already asked."
Test_With_Data: T04: limited direct dataset field; use as design requirement for escalation payload and measure via process/report outcomes.
Notes: Supports requirement to attach summary/sources/uncertainty on escalation.

Claim_Summary: Escalations should include context and show reasoning/work, even if imperfect.
Quote_or_Evidence: "If an escalation arrived saying here is the ticket, here is what I think it is about, here is the documentation that seemed relevant, and here is specifically what I was not confident about, I would be twice as fast. I do not need it to be right. I need it to show its working."
Test_With_Data: T04/T26: design and evaluate escalation payload completeness fields; tie to decision log/routing reason.
Notes: Direct input to routing/escalation artifact requirements.

Claim_Summary: Automation trained on current practices may propagate outdated/wrong knowledge from personal snippets.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Whatever you build will be trained on what we do now, and some of what we do now is wrong. There are answers circulating in people's personal snippet files that were correct two years ago and have not been right since. If you learn from those you will scale up a mistake."
Test_With_Data: T05/T26: prefer curated KB corpus (documentation.json) as retrieval source; audit coverage and avoid learning from unreviewed snippets.
Notes: Supports retrieval-grounding over imitation of historical behavior.

Claim_Summary: Security/account compromise, billing disputes, and data-location issues are high-risk categories for automation.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Anything touching security or account compromise, obviously. Billing disputes... nothing automated should be making commitments about money. And anything involving data location... the consequence is a compliance problem."
Test_With_Data: T04: identify intents/labels related to security/billing/data location and must_not_auto_respond patterns; enforce policy routing/guardrails.
Notes: Informs forced-escalation and guardrail policies.

Claim_Summary: Support KB has 29 articles covering core repeated topics.
Quote_or_Evidence: "There are twenty-nine articles in the support knowledge base... They cover the things support answers repeatedly: authentication, deployment, the API, billing, data, security, account management."
Test_With_Data: T05: inventory documentation.json and map categories/intents to doc IDs (coverage matrix).
Notes: Baseline for retrieval corpus audit.

Claim_Summary: Knowledge exists but internal search/findability prevents reuse; agents reconstruct answers from memory.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Externally, quite a lot. Internally, I do not think the support team uses them at all... I would see a ticket answered with a paragraph that was almost word for word one of my articles, reconstructed from memory rather than copied... Search. Our internal search matches on titles and exact terms, and customers do not describe problems in the words I used for the title."
Test_With_Data: T04/T05: compare doc-answerable tickets to escalation/FCR and corpus coverage; test semantic retrieval opportunity vs keyword gap.
Notes: Strong evidence that delivery/findability is central, not absence of answers.

Claim_Summary: Private snippet files are unreviewed and risky; curated KB preferred for retrieval with citations.
Quote_or_Evidence: "What worries me is what is not in there. Every agent has a private file of answers and none of that has been reviewed by anyone... If a system retrieved from your articles... I would want to know which article an answer came from, so that when an answer is wrong I can tell whether the article is wrong or the system misread it."
Test_With_Data: T05: confirm corpus as source of truth; implement citation-to-source resolution and logging.
Notes: Supports citation requirements and source traceability.

Claim_Summary: Some request types are not covered by docs (feature requests, roadmap/timing, novel incidents) and should not be answered as if grounded.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Feature requests, obviously, since there is no answer to retrieve. Anything about roadmap or timing. And genuinely novel incidents... by definition there is no article yet. That last category is small but it is the one where a wrong answer does the most damage."
Test_With_Data: T04/T05: identify intents/tickets with no supporting docs (answerable_from_docs false / missing expected_doc_ids) and require escalation or safe no-answer behavior.
Notes: Defines limits of automation and need for 'I don't know/escalate'.

Claim_Summary: Slow response is the main pain; response urgency/value differs by issue type despite same queue.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Slow but decent once you get there. The waiting is the problem... If I am asking how pagination works, I can wait... If my deployment is failing at nine in the morning... four hours is a serious problem. Same queue, completely different cost to me."
Test_With_Data: T04: segment by urgency/intent/channel and relate to response-time/CSAT baselines; prioritize high-impact cases.
Notes: Supports urgency-aware triage and business framing.

Claim_Summary: Customers often find answers in docs while waiting; eventual replies may duplicate found content, wasting time.
Quote_or_Evidence: "Search the documentation myself, usually. I find the answer maybe half the time. When I do find it, the reply that eventually arrives is normally the same thing, and I have burned two hours."
Test_With_Data: T04/T05: quantify doc-answerable share and delays; assess potential first-response improvement from grounded retrieval answers.
Notes: Reinforces documentation-delivery/findability problem from customer perspective.

Claim_Summary: Automated first responses are acceptable if honest, cited, and calibrated; confident wrong answers are unacceptable; automation should be disclosed.
Quote_or_Evidence: "If it says here is what I think, here is the page it came from, and a person will confirm, that is useful... What I would not accept is something that sounds certain and is wrong... I would want to know it was automated... because I calibrate how much I trust it."
Test_With_Data: T04/T26: measure citation accuracy/hallucination risk; define response format and escalation/confirmation behavior in PRD/prompts.
Notes: Informs answer style, citation display, and disclosure/uncertainty handling.

Claim_Summary: Service differences across customer plans/tiers are noticed and can affect renewal; changes must not worsen perceived inequity.
Quote_or_Evidence: "We are on the business plan... a colleague... on the enterprise plan... gets answers in about an hour... if this change makes that gap bigger, we will notice, and it will come up at renewal."
Test_With_Data: T04: segment baseline and system outcomes by customer_tier/region/language_fluency; include in fairness audit.
Notes: Supports tier-aware evaluation and governance.

Claim_Summary: Brief highlights that many incoming questions may already be answered in CloudServe documentation (to be discovered).
Quote_or_Evidence: "A large share of the incoming volume is made up of questions that have already been answered somewhere in CloudServe's own documentation... expected to find for yourself during discovery..."
Test_With_Data: T04/T05: test using labels.answerable_from_docs, expected_doc_ids coverage, and corpus mapping.
Notes: Hypothesis to validate with EV-09/EV-10/EV-20/EV-24 and ticket data.

Claim_Summary: Current baselines and targets frame discovery and evaluation (FCR 42%→60%+, first reply 8–12h→<5 min project target, escalation 58%→≤30%, CSAT 3.2→≥4.0).
Quote_or_Evidence: "First contact resolution 42%... 60% or better; Average time to first reply 8 to 12 hours... Under 5 minutes; Escalation rate 58%... 30% or lower; Customer satisfaction 3.2 / 5... 4.0 or better."
Test_With_Data: T04: reproduce/approximate baselines from development_tickets.json history; explain discrepancies.
Notes: Reference targets for later stages; not interview evidence.

Test_With_Data: Re-run `python scripts/eda.py`; inspect answerable_from_docs.csv and intent/channel slices.
Notes: Supports hypothesis that many tickets have existing documentation/auto-response potential; by-channel and by-intent breakdowns available in outputs.

Quote_or_Evidence: docs/workbooks/eda_outputs/contradictions_verdicts.csv; docs/workbooks/eda_outputs/eda_summary.md (C2)
